$comment: Mission 1.74.5. The second approval for the second question, after the first one was exhausted by an attempt that bounced. It sits BESIDE the packet, names it by a recomputed hash, and authorises exactly one manual send.

approval.why: Mission 1.66. An approval flag written into the frozen packet would change the artifact the operator read, and the packet's own gate asserts that the packet records no approval. That field means THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO APPROVAL and never that no approval exists.
approval.why_it_was_recomputed_rather_than_copied: the operator's message carries a digest, and copying it would make the approval name whatever the instruction said rather than whatever the packet is. Recomputing turns a quoted string into a check: if the two had disagreed the approval would have been refused rather than recorded.

approved_action.$comment: Mission 1.65's envelope rule. The digest binds the ACTION and excludes itself, the execution status, the recorded date and the sender.
approved_action.approved_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites
approved_action.why_the_sender_is_not_pinned: the operator stated the sending mailbox is chosen at execution time, which is the same property Mission 1.65 recorded in advance for a manual mail send: the sender is not determined until the send. The cost is unchanged -- this approval pins the action apart from the mailbox it leaves from.

execution.$comment: Mission 1.74.6. An approval says an action MAY be performed; this records that one WAS. What it does not record is that the message arrived, because the attestation is silent on delivery and nothing here may look.
execution.why_the_offset_matters: a naked local time names no instant, and this record is read by people who are not in the operator's timezone and cannot ask.
execution.attested_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites
execution.attestation_statement: I manually sent the approved GP-R2-Q1 v2 exactly once from thib.chm@gmail.com to d@globalping.io using the approved subject and frozen body.
execution.why_byte_verification_is_unreachable_her: still a manual mail send, so still Mission 1.66's ceiling: the send happens in a mail client nothing in this repository can observe. The channel changed from the designated address to the published one and the OBSERVABILITY did not, because the ceiling is a property of the medium rather than of the address.
execution.upgrade_path: NONE for this channel. A future mission may record OPERATOR_ATTESTED and nothing above it.
execution.reachable_only_through: an explicit operator attestation that the message was sent, plus the sending mailbox, which no frozen document contains.
attestation_covers: that it was sent exactly once
that the frozen body was used
attestation_does_not_cover: the bytes that actually left the mail client
execution.why_the_sender_is_attested_rather_than_c: the approval deliberately left the sender unbound, so no field of it constrains the mailbox and no artifact here records one. The mailbox is known because the operator said so, and that is the whole of the evidence for it. Mission 1.74.5 stated that cost in advance; this is the record of paying it.
execution.why_the_sender_was_not_written_back: back-filling the approval's sender field would make an unpinned field look pinned and make this mailbox read as approved in advance, which it was not. The approval keeps its placeholder and the execution carries the real address.
execution.why_the_body_was_not_compared: comparing what was sent against the frozen body would require reading the operator's mailbox, which nobody authorised and which Mission 1.66 refused. The frozen body is what the attestation says was used; this repository has not seen what left.

delivery.$comment: A send is an act by the sender. A delivery is an outcome at the receiver. The attestation establishes the first and is silent on the second.
delivery.why_delivery_is_unconfirmed: the attestation states that a message was sent and says nothing about whether it arrived. The operator instructed that the strongest justified state be recorded and that successful delivery not be inferred -- and this arc has already shown the difference, because the v1 message to legal@globalping.io was also sent before it bounced.
delivery.why_silence_is_not_evidence: no non-delivery report has been given to this record, and nothing here looked for one. Silence from an unexamined mailbox is not an observation, and this record was written minutes after the send, which is sooner than a bounce would necessarily arrive.

execution.why_provider_contacted_is_false: a contact means something reached the provider, and only delivery would establish that. The dispatch is attested and the delivery is not, so marking a contact here would put an event in the record that nobody observed.
execution.why_no_reply_is_recorded: none has been reported, and a reply is a document: it would be frozen verbatim in its own record before anything interpreted it. Nothing was read, and this record claims nothing about what the provider will say or whether it will say anything.
execution.why_there_is_no_message_id: the attestation carries none and the operator instructed that one not be invented or inferred. The only route to a message id runs through the sending mailbox, which nobody authorised reading, so the field is null rather than plausible.
execution.why_the_approval_is_exhausted: it authorised exactly one send and one was made. A second send to this recipient, including a resend after a bounce that has not happened yet, is a second use of a one-use approval and needs its own.

relationship_to_the_exhausted_approval.$comment: The first approval is not reused, not reinterpreted, and not repaired. It records what happened to it.
relationship_to_the_exhausted_approval.why: the recipient differs, and the recipient is a bound field, so this authorises a different action rather than extending a spent one. The two approvals name different content digests and neither can stand in for the other.

scope.why_dispatch_changes_no_verdict: the qualification answers what the provider permits, and the provider has said nothing new. A question in flight is an act by us, not evidence about them.

recommended_next_action.action: the operator waits, and if a reply arrives forwards it so it can be frozen verbatim before anything interprets it; if a non-delivery report arrives instead, that is attested and this dispatch moves to FAILED
